posts.text:
I own a small restaurant in Spring, TX. Friday at 7 used to mean the phone ringing out while every hand was on the line.

So we built an AI host for our own place. She answers every call, takes the order, reads it back and texts a link to pay. The ticket only prints once it's paid.

Made a 30-second animation of how a 7:14 PM call goes now. Happy to share what worked and what didn't if anyone's thinking about phone ordering.

Quick one for owners on DoorDash and Uber Eats: on a $26.98 order the app can take up to 30%, so up to $8.09 is gone before rent and payroll. And next time, the guest opens the app, not you.

At our place we send regulars to our own ordering link: same food, same price, no app cut. Made a short animation of the math. What share of your orders still comes through the apps?

Has anyone else had a table walk out mid-rush? We stopped it at our place by making every table order paid first: guests scan the code, order and pay at the table, and the kitchen ticket prints only after payment.

Short animation of how it works below. Curious how others handle this.

When did your best regular last order? A regular who stops coming rarely complains. They just go quiet, and in a busy week nobody notices.

At our place, the guest list flags regulars who go quiet and sends a personal note from the restaurant, timed to their own rhythm, not a blast to everyone. Short animation below. Anyone else doing win-back texts?
